name: d512-chunked-mma
repo_anchor: plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md, section 'Design notes only (no build)': "d=512 as a chunk-count change; ... Out of scope: paged/varlen decode kernel (backlog), Triton/GDN kernel work, d=512 implementation." and section 'Design notes' (2026-09-06 execution record): "d=512: a chunk-count change on the same structure (4 x 128 chains); smem stays at the 32-row KV tile size. Only worth instantiating when a shipped model demands it (Gemma-4 class)." The d=256 substrate this extends is the landed route-B kernel (same file, 'K-chunked d=256 in the bridge kernel (landed)': S = QK^T and PV each chain two 128-deep m16n8k8 sequences with fp32 accumulation across chunks; smem 33,792 B; d256 sits at 255/254 registers per the 2026-09-07 decode bisect record). Item also recorded in research/lacunae/outline.yaml (category: kernels).
current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the demand side is concrete: Gemma 4 (Google DeepMind, technical report arXiv:2607.02770, 2026-07-02; sizes E2B/E4B/12B/26B-A4B/31B) interleaves 5 local sliding-window layers with head_dim=256 per 1 global full-attention layer (4:1 for E2B); per flash-attention #2427 (2026-04-02, open) the global layers run head_dim=512 with 8 query / 4 KV heads in the config tested (indices 3, 9, 15, 21 of 30 layers; the 31B NVFP4 build reports GQA group size 8 on globals per vLLM #48082). The tech report adds two kernel-relevant facts: global layers reuse keys as values (V=K, except E2B/E4B, 'up to 37.5%' global-KV saving) and use pp-RoPE (p=0.25) vs standard RoPE on locals. Supply side: FA2 hard-caps at 256 everywhere (runtime error 'FlashAttention only supports head dimensions up to 256'; PyPI page confirms max 256) — no 512 branch exists or is planned; FA3/FA4 cute kernels gate on cc >= 8.0 excluding 8.6/8.9 and depend on Hopper TMA+WGMMA (flash-attention #2581, 2026-05-21); FA4 RFC #2456 (2026-04-13) merged head_dim=256 for SM100/SM110 Blackwell but head_dim=512 is Phase-4 'planned, no branches', and per vLLM #48082 FA4 itself falls back to FA2 at 512 on SM100 due to a TMEM limit. The only shipped head_dim=512 serving path is vLLM PR #38822 (merged 2026-05-23): head_dim 512 added to the FlashInfer TRTLLM-gen backend, via SM100f-only cubins (BF16/FP8/FP16, FlashInfer PR #2959) — Blackwell-only, later found to cover only a subset of 512-wide specializations (vLLM #48082, Gemma-4 MTP crash on B200 'Trtllm-gen kernels not found', workaround --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN; gating PR #49917). vLLM's own Gemma4 config force-locks TRITON_ATTN for the whole model 'to prevent mixed-backend numerical divergence' (vLLM #38887, 2026-04-03: E4B at ~9 tok/s on RTX 4090 vs 100+ for Llama 3.2 3B; the per-layer selection fix PR #38891 is still open with evals showing near-identical accuracy). Engine-level: heterogeneous 256/512 per-layer page sizes raise NotImplementedError at vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1035 ('The page size of the layer is not divisible by the maximum page size') — vLLM #41403 (2026-04-30) tracks it as the hard 5th gate, with fix PRs #39931 (LCM block-size padding, open) and #40391. Pre-sm80 precedents for 512-deep QK^T/PV mma chains are strong: llama.cpp master ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-mma-f16.cuh ships a dedicated ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_turing table instantiating (DKQ,DV) = (256,256), (320,256), (512,512), (576,512) for sm_75 with Q_in_reg=false and nstages=1 (no cp.async below sm_80), including a V_is_K_view code path for MLA-style K-as-V and logit_softcap; and flash-attention #1483 'FFPA' (2025-02-09, DefTruth) demonstrates MMA-level chunked tiling over the head dim (demonstrated to D=1024, m16n8k16 atoms, tested Volta through Ada) hitting 105/119 = 88% of peak on L20 at D=512 with fp32 accumulation.
sm75_viability: Nothing upstream serves d=512 on Turing today; measured state of every candidate on this host (Quadro RTX 6000, sm_75): FA2 — d=512 not in its template set; its sub-sm80 bodies are additionally disqualified by plan/0007 gate 0 (d=256 fp16 causal: LAUNCH FAILURE cudaErrorInvalidValue, d=256 smem demand exceeds Turing's 64 KiB block cap; d=128: launches but SILENTLY WRONG, max_err 2.20 vs two agreeing references). FlashInfer 0.6.18 — no 512 anywhere on sm_75 (TRTLLM-gen cubins are SM100-only) and vLLM's FlashInfer backend raised its capability floor to (8,0) with the comment that FlashInfer 'is currently broken on SM75 (Turing)'; locally its decode was the only correct third-party baseline at d=256 (16.2 tok/s b=1 kv=1024, 11.8 at kv=4096) but prefill was gate-0 disqualified as silently wrong (max_err up to 4.24). TRITON_ATTN — the path vLLM force-locks for all of Gemma 4; on sm_75 its math ceiling is the Triton codegen path: triton #189 shows tl.dot historically lowered to Volta mma.884 at half Turing-native mma.1688 throughput, and triton #5066 dropped Volta/Turing support entirely since Triton 3.3, so modern triton emits no tensor-core math on sm_75 (scalar/FMA level throughput; community measurements show tl.dot at scalar-arithmetic levels) — the lane therefore pins triton <=3.2, leaving mma.884 half-throughput at best; a d=512 QK^T on that path is FMA-bound end to end. FLEX_ATTENTION — Triton-based, same codegen floor. The viable sm_75 answer is the fork's BRIDGE_ATTN: the landed k-chunked d=256 kernel already chains two 128-deep m16n8k8 sequences with fp32 accumulation at 22.0-24.3 TFLOP/s (on par per-FLOP with d=128), and d=512 is a chunk-count change (4 x 128 chains) per plan/0007. Real capability floors for the 512 instantiation: (1) register wall — d=256 already sits at 255/254 registers/lane (the accumulator wall: 128 fp32 O-accumulator regs/lane), so a d=512 output row doubles O-lane pressure and cannot ride 16-row tiles without spills; llama.cpp's turing 512/512 table answers this by splitting Q rows across ncols1 x ncols2 sub-tiles (8-64 cols per block, 64-256 threads, occupancy 1-4, Q_in_reg=false). (2) smem cap — naive scaling of the 32-row KV tile would need 2 x 32 KiB + misc ~ 66.5 KiB > Turing's 64 KiB block cap; fixes are 16-row tiles or the V_is_K_view trick (Gemma 4 globals are literally V=K for the larger models, so one tile serves both GEMMs, exactly the llama.cpp MLA path). (3) no cp.async below sm_80 — single-stage loads (nstages=1), already the pattern in both the bridge kernel and llama.cpp's turing table. Attention-backend candidate matrix for d=512 on sm_75: FLASH_ATTN no (cap 256 + gate-0 broken sub-sm80), FLASHINFER no (SM100 cubins only, sm_75 floor raised to 8.0), TRITON_ATTN runs but FMA/half-mma math, FLEX_ATTENTION same Triton floor, BRIDGE_ATTN yes after this item lands.
upstream_base: Dated ledger lines the fork can rebase onto: 2025-02-09 flash-attention #1483 opens FFPA (chunked-headdim MMA tiling, Volta-Ada, D up to 1024) — design precedent only, never merged. 2026-04-02 flash-attention #2427 opens head_dim=512 request (Gemma 4); open, no PR, no maintainer response. 2026-04-03 vLLM #38887 documents Gemma4 forced TRITON_ATTN (9 tok/s E4B/4090); same-day PR #38891 (per-layer backend selection) still open as of July 2026 (needs-rebase). 2026-04-13 flash-attention RFC #2456: FA4 head_dim=256 merged for SM100/110 (PRs #2412, #2487); 512 remains Phase-4 planned. 2026-04-30 vLLM #41403 tracks the heterogeneous 256/512 page-size NotImplementedError (kv_cache_utils.py:1035); fix PRs #39931 (LCM padding, open) and #40391. 2026-05-21 flash-attention #2581 (SM89 512 request) confirms FA3/FA4 exclude 8.6/8.9. 2026-05-23 vLLM PR #38822 merges head_dim=512 for FlashInfer TRTLLM attention (SM100f cubins via FlashInfer PR #2959; fp8 .view bridge for the NVFP4 reinterpretation bug). 2026-07-02 Gemma 4 technical report arXiv:2607.02770. 2026-07-09 vLLM #48082 (512 cubin subset gap on B200 MTP; workaround TRITON_ATTN; references gating PR #49917). Triton lineage: #189 (Volta mma.884 half-throughput on Turing, long-standing) and #5066 (Volta/Turing dropped since 3.3) — the lane's triton <=3.2 pin. llama.cpp master carries the ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_turing table (256/256, 320/256, 512/512, 576/512) as the living reference implementation; last-good for this host remains the fork's own plan/0007 d=256 kernel (bridge_attn scope {64,128,256}, 18/18 backend suite green) since no upstream release has ever shipped an sm_75 d=512 attention.
effort_estimate: Full campaign but a bounded one — bigger than a registry row, smaller than plan/0007 itself. Kernel ladder entry: D=512 template on the existing flash_fwd_sm75.cuh structure (4 x 128-deep m16n8k8 chains for S and PV, fp32 accumulation across chunks) plus the two capability floors that make it more than a pure chunk-count change: an O-accumulator tile split (ncols1/ncols2 sub-tiling a la llama.cpp turing 512/512) to survive the 255-register wall, and either 16-row KV tiles or a V=K single-tile view to fit Turing's 64 KiB smem cap. Oracle extension first (d=512 cases: MHA, GQA 2:1 (8Q/4KV) and 8:1 (31B shape), causal/full, chunked prefix, magnitude regressions). Then shim/scope/test updates (bridge_attn.py scope + 512), ptxas zero-spill assert, bench, and — if engine serving is in scope — the heterogeneous 256/512 KV-page layout work in the engine (per-layer page sizes or LCM padding) which is realistically its own sub-campaign. Rough size: the plan/0007 d=256 step (kernel+oracle+bench+integration in one day of gate-run execution) times 1.5-2.5 for the retile risk, plus the page-size engine work if targeted.
unlocks: Gemma 4 family end-to-end on sm_75 (E4B through 31B): the 5-in-6 sliding layers already ride the landed d=256 bridge kernel, so this item closes the remaining 1-in-6 global layers and removes the TRITON_ATTN force-lock that would otherwise FMA-bind the entire model on this host. Structurally, the same k-chunked instantiation covers the MLA tuples (576/512, 320/256) — DeepSeek-class asymmetric (qk, v) shapes — by chunking the K axis independently of the V axis, per the plan/0007 design note and the llama.cpp turing table which already ships exactly those tuples. Also unblocks heterogeneous 256/512 engine serving (the #41403 page-size class of problem) for any hybrid model, and is the operator's only path to d=512 prefill numerics that pass gate 0 on Turing (every upstream alternative is either silently wrong, unlaunchable, SM100-only, or FMA-bound).
dependency_order: Must land first: nothing new — the plan/0007 d=256 bridge kernel (landed 2026-09-06, macro-gate methodology fixed 2026-09-07) is the substrate; the fp64 oracle harness already exists and extends by case-adding. External prerequisites: none (CUDA 13.3 lane toolchain in place; no triton dependency for the kernel itself). Ordering inside the item: (1) oracle d=512 cases before any kernel timing (gate 0 discipline); (2) D=512 template with tile split / V=K view, zero-spill assert; (3) llama.cpp fattn-mma 512/512 sm_75 run as the independent adjudication reference can proceed in parallel with (1)-(2); (4) bridge_attn scope + backend tests; (5) engine-side heterogeneous page-size handling (mirroring vLLM #39931 LCM padding or per-layer page sizes) must precede any Gemma 4 engine gate; (6) d=512 decode shape after prefill (the plan/0007 paged/varlen decode backlog constrains decode either way). Parallelizable: (3) and the model-adapter work (pp-RoPE on globals, V=K plumbing, softcap already hooked) carry no kernel dependency.
risk_notes: Correctness/numerics: (1) accumulation order — 4 chunks of fp32 accumulation per 16x8 tile changes summation order vs the d=128 kernel and vs any fp16-PV reference; the fp64 oracle absorbs this but the fp16-saturation magnitude regressions must be re-run at d=512 because QK^T sums 512 products before the fp32-subtract-before-h2exp2 invariant applies; (2) silently-wrong fallbacks are the dominant hazard on this host (FA2 sub-sm80 d=128 and FlashInfer prefill were both gate-0 disqualified in plan/0007) — any 'it launches' result without the differential check is worthless; (3) V=K view is only valid for the Gemma 4 sizes that reuse keys as values (not E2B/E4B), so the tile-reuse optimization must be config-gated or the 16-row-tile variant is the safe default. Performance risks: the 255-register wall (d=256 already at 255/254) means spills are likely without the ncols split — ptxas spill count must be a hard assert, with the llama.cpp fp16-PV-accumulator variant as the flagged fallback; single-stage loads (no cp.async on sm_75) double the exposure to load latency at 4x the chain depth. Upstream-drift exposure: low for the kernel (no upstream sm_75 d=512 exists to drift against — this is the fork's own surface), moderate for the engine adapter (vLLM Gemma4 forcing, #38891/#39931/#49917 all in flight, so the fork's vLLM lane will see churn in exactly the config-selection and page-size code this touches).
determinism_class: Kernel-side: bitwise deterministic run-to-run for a fixed launch configuration — the prefill forward uses no atomics and no split-K; the k-chunked accumulation order is a compile-time constant (4 x 128 chain), and softmax rescaling rides the same fp32 KQ_max/KQ_rowsum discipline as d=256. The chunk-count change does alter the fp32 rounding profile vs d=128 (different partial-sum boundaries), so the per-d error envelope must be re-measured against the fp64 oracle rather than inherited — statistical, not bitwise, equivalence across d. Restart-to-restart variance on this host is engine-level, not kernel-level (plan/0007's 2026-09-07 records: tp2 decode rows swing 12.4-16.4 tok/s between engine restarts of the same kernel; kernel-isolated A/B is stable), so the float64-oracle + median-of-N gate discipline — medians across at least three engine restarts for tp2 arms, per-row rep spreads recorded — is what keeps performance judgments honest; correctness gates remain single-run asserts because the kernel is bitwise stable.
priority_signal: For: the model list is no longer hypothetical — Gemma 4 shipped April 2026 with head_dim=512 globals, and nothing upstream will ever serve that dim on sm_75 (FA2 capped at 256 with no plan, FA3/FA4 gated cc>=8.0 excluding even Ada, FlashInfer's 512 exists only as SM100 cubins and its vLLM backend floor is now SM80, Triton is FMA/no-mma on sm_75 since 3.3) — so the window is not closing, it is permanently open for lack of any competitor, which also means zero upstream-drift risk on the kernel surface. The precedent stack is unusually strong (llama.cpp turing table ships 512/512 and 576/512 on sm_75 today; FFPA proved 88% of peak at D=512 with fp32 accumulation on pre-Hopper parts), and the incremental cost rides a landed, gate-tested d=256 kernel. Against: only the minority global layers benefit (1 in 6 layers; the 5-in-6 sliding layers are already served), so operator value hinges on actually wanting Gemma 4 in the serving mix; the register/smem retile makes 'just a chunk-count change' optimistic; and engine serving additionally requires the heterogeneous page-size work (#41403 class) that is a real sub-campaign of its own. Net: high-value if Gemma 4 is on the operator's model list, deferrable without decay otherwise.
recommended_probe: Gate-0 probe, no timing until numerics are proven: (1) extend the fp64 oracle with d=512 cases (MHA, GQA 2:1 and 8:1, causal/full, chunked prefix, magnitude regressions) and freeze tolerances from the fp64 reference; (2) instantiate the D=512 template with the conservative 16-row KV tile (no V=K view yet) and the ncols-style O-accumulator split, compile with the ptxas zero-spill assert — if spills survive all splits, record the blocker before any benchmark; (3) differential-check against torch fp32/fp64 einsum AND a second agreeing reference (llama.cpp fattn-mma 512/512 built for sm_75 is the natural second witness since its turing table ships exactly this shape); (4) only then, three bench points (s=2048/8192, b=1 decode-shaped) judged on per-FLOP parity with the d=256 rows (22.0/24.3 TFLOP/s), median-of-N per the cross-restart methodology. Success criterion: oracle ALL PASS with a max_err profile matching the d=64/128/256 family, zero spills, per-FLOP throughput within ~15% of the d=256 kernel — anything else is recorded as a blocker, not tuned around.
